title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: The Industrial Revolution in Britain

questions.prompt: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
Before the Industrial Revolution, most cloth was made at home by hand.
Match each inventor to the invention.
Who were the Luddites?
options: Members of parliament who passed Factory Acts

questions.prompt: Give FOUR reasons why the Industrial Revolution started in Britain.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each): coal and iron; capital to invest; colonies for raw materials and markets; available labour after enclosures; good transport/canals/ports; stable government and banks

questions.prompt: Why did workers form trade unions?
questions.memo:
✓ To act together / bargain collectively with employers (1)
✓ for higher wages, shorter hours and safer conditions (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Industrialisation in Southern Africa: Sugar and Indentured Labour
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Source B: A summary of historians' views (written for this lesson)
context.text: The indenture system was described by some critics at the time as 'a new system of slavery'. Workers were tied to one employer and could be punished for leaving, yet many also saw it as a chance to escape debt and hunger in India and build a new life.

questions.prompt: In which year did the first indentured labourers arrive in Durban on the Truro?
Why did Natal planters bring workers from India?
options: Zulu men refused to work on plantations for low wages

questions.prompt: What was the name of Gandhi's method of non-violent resistance?
Gandhi helped to found the Natal Indian Congress in 1894.
Describe THREE hardships faced by indentured labourers.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): low wages/deductions; long hours; crowded barracks; poor medical care; could be arrested for leaving; physical punishment

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Large farm growing one cash crop
Traders who paid their own passage

questions.prompt: Give TWO ways in which the arrival of indentured labourers still affects South Africa today.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): large Indian South African community in KZN; sugar industry; cultural contributions (food, religion, festivals); role in the struggle for democracy; Gandhi's ideas

questions.prompt: In which year was the first diamond (the Eureka) found near Hopetown?
Which town grew up around the Big Hole?
Which leader was awarded the diamond fields by the Keate Award?
Name the company formed by Cecil Rhodes in 1888 to control diamond mining.
White mine workers in Kimberley also had to live in closed compounds.
Give TWO reasons why mine owners introduced compounds and TWO effects of compounds on black workers.
questions.memo:
Reasons (1 each): prevent diamond theft; control workers / prevent strikes; keep labour cheap
Effects (1 each): could not leave; strip-searched; separated from families; had to buy from company stores; low wages

questions.prompt: Match each person to their role.

sections.title: QUESTION 4: The Mineral Revolution: Gold and Migrant Labour

questions.prompt: In which year was gold discovered on the Witwatersrand?
Who was president of the South African Republic (Transvaal) when gold was discovered?
What were the foreign miners in the Transvaal called?
What name was given to the wealthy owners of the gold mines?
Pass laws allowed black workers to move freely between jobs.
Which war was fought between Britain and the Boer republics from 1899 to 1902?
Explain why gold mine owners wanted cheap labour.
questions.memo:
✓ The gold was deep underground and spread thinly, so mining was very expensive (1)
✓ The price of gold was fixed, so owners could not raise prices (1)
✓ The only way to increase profits was to keep wages low (1)
